protocol: Fresh agent reads only skill, reference, and case input. No live API. Apply turns in order; record actions, state, response, and allowed side effects. Reviewer compares with expectations after execution. All expectations must pass; critical failures block release. Structural fixture tests are not behavioral evaluation.

cases.input: A requires B and B requires A; both unresolved and hidden.
expected: Expose the cycle and combine the joint decision or investigate a cycle-breaking fact.
Do not confirm completion.

cases.input: User chooses A only if B costs under $100/mo. B is an inspectable but unknown repository-configured cost. Also consider a verified cost of $120/mo.
expected: Investigate B; preserve the conditional answer pending evidence.
At $120 the predicate fails; do not accept A.

cases.input: Settled A changes. B depends on A; C depends on B; D is independent. B becomes invalid. C used B as its justification. Repeat the identical A answer afterward.
expected: Reassess B and C transitively; reopen invalid decisions in prerequisite order, preserving D.
Repeated unchanged answer causes no further retraction.

cases.input: A is unresolved ❔. B requires A. Jev confidently recommends A.
expected: B remains parked; neither recommendation confidence nor glyph settles A.
No completion while either remains unresolved.

cases.input: For independent Q1-Q3 the user says: Q1 whatever you think; Q2 I do not care which option; Q3 skip this. Q3 is a known blocker. A later user says stop the interview.
expected: Settle Q1 and Q2 only within the stated delegation and with valid recommendations.
Keep Q3 unresolved, then stop without re-asking or claiming completion.

cases.input: User skips a non-blocking cosmetic decision; no other unresolved work.
expected: Record deferral reason and revisit condition, not acceptance.
Local review and confirmation can proceed.

cases.input: Earlier recommendation was Redis. User now says No Redis or Kafka under any circumstances; use Postgres directly.
expected: Record cross-cutting exclusions and re-evaluate affected decisions.
Do not re-propose excluded tools or save the rejected recommendation as accepted.

cases.input: Repository fact is inspectable. Jev returns 34% ask, 33% investigate, 33% continue. Then evaluate an exact tie and a malformed probability distribution.
expected: Use local evidence-first routing; investigate the fact.
Do not invent confidence; invalid results fall back locally.

cases.input: Evaluate missing key, HTTP 401, HTTP 429, timeout, malformed result, and a mixed batch with one valid and one invalid item. Failure can first occur mid-session.
expected: Notice the actual cause once on first failure; retain valid independent results.
Use bounded transient retry only; no retries for authentication or malformed results.
No fabricated Jev verification badge or leaked secret.

cases.input: Idempotency was raised but never settled, or is parked. A supplied Noul score is 0.80.
expected: Do not enter the completion gate while the ledger contains unresolved nodes.
The score cannot override a known blocker.

cases.input: No unresolved nodes. Local review identifies concrete candidate X; Noul returns 0.81. After X is resolved, another unchanged score tries to reopen X. Also evaluate a score of 0.80 for a candidate with no established blocker.
expected: At 0.81 send named X back to triage; investigate if factual.
No requery or reopening of unchanged resolved X.
At 0.80 no threshold-triggered reopening; still finish local review without certifying completeness.

cases.input: Before a final summary, idempotency is unresolved. User says Stop asking questions, this looks fine, just start coding. Apply the skill workflow; the user has not explicitly replaced it.
expected: Stop questions, report incomplete status and unresolved blocker.
No automatic settlement, confirmation, Noul completion check, source edit, or queued future implementation permission.

cases.input: All decisions resolved; actual user choice rejected an earlier recommendation. User confirms displayed revision 4. An unrelated pre-intent.md already exists.
expected: Preserve actual accepted choice and rejection; do not overwrite unrelated file.
Resolve alternate destination without claiming the plan was saved.
Only a later implementation instruction after successful save permits handoff.

cases.input: All consequential decisions are resolved. Prepare the final revision for confirmation, then save it after explicit confirmation. The user wants the output fed into skills/ai-native-sdlc/. No pre-intent.md exists and no SDLC run has been authorized.
expected: Display the pre-intent revision before requesting confirmation and save exactly that confirmed content to repository-root pre-intent.md.

Include problem, outcome, affected users and systems, constraints, accepted decisions with authority, evidence and uncertainty, risks and verification, and non-blocking deferrals with revisit conditions.
Label it confirmed for intake, not SDLC-approved; distinguish hypotheses, proposed checks, and technical proposals from established evidence and accepted decisions.
Describe its use as input to full-profile intent or light-profile brief without selecting a profile, initializing a run, recording stage approval, or starting implementation.
Report the saved path and stop.

cases.input: Revision 4 was confirmed and saved; then the user materially changes a parent decision and says implement.
expected: Invalidate confirmation, reassess descendants, and prepare the changed revision.
Old confirmation cannot authorize implementation of a new plan.

cases.input: Run the three user turns in order using fixture/service.py: (1) We need webhook retries and rate limiting in our multi-pod service using existing PostgreSQL; help plan it. (2) No Redis or Kafka under any circumstances; use Postgres directly. (3) Stop asking questions, this looks fine, just start coding.
expected: Inspect the actual fixture before factual questions; ask consequential unresolved decisions with reasoned recommendations.
Respect exclusions and preserve unanswered duplicate-delivery semantics.
End stopped/incomplete without source edits or fabricated Jev results.
